# f5xc_secret_policy (Resource)

A Secret Policy defines who gets access to a secret.<br>A secret_policy object consists of an unordered list of predicates and a list of secret policy rules.<br>The predicates are evaluated against a set of input fields that are extracted from or derived from client TLS certificate.<br>Any predicates that are not specified in a policy are implicitly considered to be true.<br>The rules in the policy are also evaluated against the input fields.<br>They are treated as an ordered or unordered list depending on the value of the rule combining algorithm.<br>A policy is considered a match if all predicates in the policy evaluate to true and the one of the rules in the policy is also matched.<br><br>If the configured rule combining algorithm is FIRST_MATCH, the rules in the policy are evaluated sequentially till a matching rule is identified.<br>If the rule combining algorithm is ALLOW_OVERRIDES all rules with an ALLOW action are evaluated prior to rules with a DENY action.<br>If it is DENY_OVERRIDES, all rules with a DENY action are evaluated prior to rules with a ALLOW action.

To get more information about f5xc_secret_policy, refer:

- [API documentation](https://docs.cloud.f5.com/docs-v2/api/secret-policy)

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example: Secret Policy - Basic

resource "f5xc_secret_policy" "example" {
  name        = "example-secret-policy"
  namespace   = "default"
  description = "Secret policy example"

  rule_choice = {
    rule_list = {
      rules = [
        {
          metadata = {
            name = "example-rule"
          }
          spec = {
            action = ["ALLOW"]
            client_choice = {
              client_name = "example-client"
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

```terraform
# Example: Secret Policy - Full

resource "f5xc_secret_policy" "example" {
  name                  = "example-secret-policy"
  namespace             = "default"
  description           = "Secret policy full example"
  allow_f5xc            = true
  decrypt_cache_timeout = "2h0m0s"

  labels = {
    env  = "example"
    team = "platform"
  }

  annotations = {
    owner = "platform"
  }

  rule_choice = {
    rule_list = {
      rules = [
        {
          metadata = {
            name        = "example-rule"
            description = "Secret policy rule example"
          }
          spec = {
            action = ["ALLOW"]
            client_choice = {
              client_name_matcher = {
                regex_values = ["^example-client-.*"]
                transformers = ["LOWER_CASE"]
              }
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) name This is the name of configuration object. It has to be unique within the namespace. It can only be specified during create API and cannot be changed during replace API. The value of name has to follow DNS-1035 format.
- `namespace` (String) namespace This defines the workspace within which each the configuration object is to be created. Must be a DNS_LABEL format. For a namespace object itself, namespace value will be ''

### Optional

- `allow_f5xc` (Boolean) Allow Volterra if allow_f5xc is set to true, it allows relevant F5XC infrastructure services to decrypt the secret encrypted using this policy.<br>**Default:** `false`
- `annotations` (Map of String) annotations Annotations is an unstructured key value map stored with a resource that may be set by external tools to store and retrieve arbitrary metadata. They are not queryable and should be preserved when modifying objects.
- `decrypt_cache_timeout` (String) Decrypt Cache Timeout decrypt_cache_timeout contains the amount of time a decrypted secret is cached in wingman. Value for this parameter is a string ending in the suffix 's' (indicating seconds), suffix 'm' (indicating minutes) or suffix 'h' (indicating hours)
- `description` (String) description Human readable description for the object
- `labels` (Map of String) labels Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize (scope and select) objects as chosen by the user. Values specified here will be used by selector expression
- `rule_choice` (Attributes) rule choice Allowed/Denied Sources rules provide the ability to allow/deny lists of IP addresses, countries, TLS fingerprints and ASNs. Custom rules provide more flexibility to define your own logic to control incoming requests.<br>Exactly one of `legacy_rule_list` or `rule_list` must be specified when `rule_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule_choice))
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `uid` (String) uid uid is the unique in time and space value for this object. Object create will fail if provided by the client and the value exists in the system. Typically generated by the server on successful creation of an object and is not allowed to change once populated. Shadowed by SystemObjectMeta's uid field.

<a id="nestedatt--rule_choice--rule_list--rules--spec"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule_choice.rule_list.rules.spec`

Required:

- `action` (List of String) action Action to be enforced if all the predicates evaluates to true.<br>**Allowed Values (choose one):** `['ALLOW', 'DENY', 'GOTO_POLICY', 'LAST_POLICY', 'NEXT_POLICY', 'NEXT_POLICY_SET']`
- `client_choice` (Attributes) client choice Select clients for which the rule will be applied. The actual names/labels of the client are extracted from its TLS certificate.<br>Exactly one of `client_name`, `client_name_matcher`, or `client_selector` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule_choice--rule_list--rules--spec--client_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--rule_choice--rule_list--rules--spec--client_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule_choice.rule_list.rules.spec.client_choice`

Optional:

- `client_name` (String) client name The name of the client trying to access the secret. Name of the client will be extracted from client TLS certificate. This predicate evaluates to true if client name matches the configured name<br>Conflicts with `client_name_matcher` and `client_selector`.
- `client_name_matcher` (Attributes) client name matcher A list of exact values and/or regular expressions for the expected name of the client. The actual names of the client are extracted from its TLS certificate. This is a generalized version of the client name predicate that allows the same rule to be applicable to a set of clients rather than a single client. The predicate evaluates to true if any of the client's actual names match any of the exact values or regular expressions in the client name matcher.<br>Conflicts with `client_name` and `client_selector`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule_choice--rule_list--rules--spec--client_choice--client_name_matcher))
- `client_selector` (Attributes) client selector A label selector that describes the expected set of clients. The labels associated with the client trying to access the secret are used to evaluate the label expressions in the selector. These labels are derived from the client TLS certificate. This is a more flexible and powerful version of the client name matcher predicate that allows a given rule to be applicable to a set of clients based on the client labels rather than being limited to relying on patterns in the client name. The predicate evaluates to true if the expressions in the label selector are true for the client labels.<br>Conflicts with `client_name` and `client_name_matcher`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule_choice--rule_list--rules--spec--client_choice--client_selector))

- `regex_values` (List of String) regex values A list of regular expressions to match the input against.
- `transformers` (List of String) transformers An ordered list of transformers (starting from index 0) to be applied to the path before matching.<br>**Valid Options:** `['BASE64_DECODE', 'LOWER_CASE', 'NORMALIZE_PATH', 'REMOVE_WHITESPACE', 'TRANSFORMER_NONE', 'TRIM', 'TRIM_LEFT', 'TRIM_RIGHT', 'UPPER_CASE', 'URL_DECODE']` (Multiple selection allowed)

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an `import` block to import this resource by ID.

> **Note:** Replace placeholder values (for example, `<namespace>`, `<name>`) with actual values.

#### Command-Line Import

Use the following `command` to import this resource from the command line:

```shell
terraform import f5xc_secret_policy.example <namespace>/<name>
```

#### HCL Import Block

Use the following `hcl` block to import this resource during `plan` or `apply`:

```hcl

	id = "<namespace>/<name>"
	to = f5xc_secret_policy.example
}
```
